title: Snow halation
review: Was my favorite love live song for a while. Turns out I'm pretty normie in that regard. Either way, trying to learn animenz's version of this on piano is something I try every December to no avail. One distinct memory I have of this song is listening to it on loop on my iPod touch the last night of summer 2014 all night until a couple hours before school started to do the AP composition homework I somehow procrastinated doing until the very last moment (somehow didn't fail that assignment, but still ended up being the only grade below A I got during high school)

title: 無敵のSoldier
review: The song that started my love for music. Introduced to me by my sister, I wasn't really invested in any song before until this one. It's the way that the song was an absolute banger, while also telling a touching story. After listening to this song, I ended up listening to the rest of the album, and eventually fell down the youtube rabbit hole of other Japanese songs until I was only listening to Japanese music.

title: メクルメ
review: Fascinating song musically, that seems to say at lot at once while also saying nothing at all. A sort of self-aware naive philosophy being conveyed in an awkward and clumsy fashion (it's the image song of a character I'm unfamiliar with). Something about the song does it for me somehow, and I love it.

title: Q
review: Absolutely haunting. Of powapowa-p's discography, this song always makes it into my playlist the most, and it always evokes complicated emotions. The classic rock combined with the light glockenspiel illustrate an innocent childlike angst, followed by a form of quiet resignation. We will never know the meaning of the title, whether it is a homophone for the japanese word for "suffering", whether Q stands for question reflecting mental turbulence, or both. In the case of the latter, knowledge of the answer is haunting, for it illustrates a tragic resolve.

title: ワンダー
review: r-906 has done it again, but this time with a new retro, disco vibe (and catchy chorus). I sorta get the vibe that the theme of the song is escapism, calling to an upbeat backrooms-esque aesthetic. In a way this goes hand-in-hand with Fisher's hauntology, the feeling of being trapped in time long past.

title: ray (超かぐや姫！ Version)
review: Movie version of an old Bump of Chicken song, also one of those songs that got my to actually go and watch the source. Usually don't care much for covers in anime, but this one seemed to capture a certain energy not captured by the original (and prosekai version). Before watching, only knowing the context of the original Kaguya-hime story, I got the impression that this song was a sort of optimistic masking of some a sad departure. After watching the movie, it's immediately recontextualized as a clear celebration. Simple song, but quality storytelling.

title: 君が僕を嗤う日
review: Beautiful cover of a song from an producer that wasn't on my radar. Falls in a "bittersweet" type of song nodding towards a sort of nostalgia. The pen scratches in the quiet last verse is absolute ASMR, juxtaposed directly with the high wpm singing in the chorus, it evokes a sort of shift from sweet remembrance to a reluctant distance (temporal, spatial, or interperonal, lots of room for interpretation).

title: かなしばりに遭ったら
review: A well performed cover that captures much of the texture and tone from avaraya's original. Stilted, syncopated vocals with distortion effects to make the voice feel artificial, which, in conjunction with the dialogue at the end, paint a nightmarish conflict between dreams and reality.

attribution: ずっと真夜中でいいのに。
review: Although I love basically all of zutomayo's discography, I've pretty much settled on this one as my favorite. It's a very simple piece, and it's hard to describe why I resonate with this song so much. Thematically, I interpret this as an admittance of and disconnection, while finding personal satisfaction within oneself. It's a sort of paradox where loneliness is solved inside of one's self, which itself causes a moment of levity in it's ridiculousness.

title: ロスタルジー
review: An underrated cover artist covering a song by an underrated producer. This song perfectly conveys the "bitter" part of "bittersweet" in the genre of songs about nostalgia. There are so many sour parts throughout the song, where the melody seems to disagree with the accompaniment, almost abnormally flat at times and it's absolutely so tasteful. Hotaru does masterful emotional singing at the bridge and final chorus, making the climax actually feel satisfying and conclusive, tying directly to the satisfaction from closing the book on a nostalgia trip.

title: アストロノーツ
review: A deeply emotionally charged song. It wasn't long after I listened to this cover that I discovered that it's original producer powapowa-p passed away. It was among the first times I had to confront mortality and impermanence. The song's theme somehow also addresses these themes, with the core theme of regrets originating from one's own weakness. A core memory I have of this song is that it was the song I was listening to while watching the lane markings pass by on the highway moving out to college. I don't know my exact mind state at the time, but I remember the sadness I felt while listening to this song at that moment.

review: My absolute favorite song at the moment I was transitioning to adult life in college. At a critical period in my life, listening to this song really calmed me down, and assured me that no matter how hard things were I was never alone. Listening to it now still retains those sentiments for me.

review: Song aged amazingly. A charming adaptation of "The Boy who Cried Wolf" as part of sasakure.uk's concept album "The Fantastic Reality of Aesop". Simple instrumentation and motifs capture the innocence of the protagonist. The bridge captures a somewhat clumsy yet sad regret, but the simple innocence continues, epitomized by the "ああだいきらいです" at the end.

title: 妄想税
review:
I would say this song was actually the genesis to my interest in music in general. So basically what happened is probably somewhere in 2012 at the beginning of high school, I feel asleep on the sofa while watching some livestream. When I eventually woke up some time past midnight, the stream I was watching ended and ended up hosting this other stream of a guy playing some modded level of I wanna be the boshy with the original vocaloid version of this song playing. It was my first real exposure to vocaloid, and I dug it. After that time, I didn't know what game or song it was, but it was always a question in the back of my mind what song that was. It wasn't until roughly 2015 after already being engrossed in Japanese music that while listening to REOL songs, I rediscovered this song.

Anyways, all around catchy, and the added rap sections are actual bangers. They really somehow snuck in the credits into the song lol.

title: 恋のヒメヒメぺったんこ
ツインテール・ドリーマー!
ハッピーシンセサイザ
ウィーニーウォーカー
限りなく灰色へ
review: I'll never know if I really was depressed, but if I was, this song really captures that feeling for me. Envy, wasted potential, imposter syndrome, and an outlook that feels completely devoid of color. Two lines in particular resonate with me. "まだ人生終わっていない" 諦めんなって誰かの声", where words of encouragement ring hollow, and somehow have the opposite affect. As if knowing people have hopes in you remind you that you are letting everyone, including yourself down. "この感情奪って去ってよ", capturing the feeling that nevertheless, these feelings are deeply ingrained, hurting while also being grasped at as a form of desperate comfort. It's a cry for help, while paradoxically shrugging away the encouragement you already receive.
